summary_hint: State foster-care verification for foster parent Dana Lee — $1,240/month, active placement since 06/2023, expected to continue 3+ years.

typed_core.name: government_agency_or_provider
typed_core.why: identity — the paying agency (flattened from entity); source validation

typed_core.name: agency_contact_phone
typed_core.why: processor — reverification contact (flattened from agency_contact_information object)

typed_core.name: recipient_or_foster_parent_name
typed_core.why: identity — whose income (flattened from person[]); borrower match

typed_core.name: recipient_or_foster_parent_count
typed_core.why: disambiguator — number of recipients; flags a bad name split

typed_core.name: case_provider_or_account_number_masked
typed_core.why: PII (restricted) — case/provider number; account grouping key

typed_core.name: program_or_payment_type
typed_core.why: identity — which benefit program the payment falls under

typed_core.name: placement_start_date
typed_core.why: processor — establishes payment history length (2-year lookback)

typed_core.name: payment_frequency
typed_core.why: disambiguator — monthly vs per-diem vs annual; without it the amount is unreadable
typed_core.prompt_hint: A per-diem/per-child rate must be captured with its unit — do not annualize at extraction

typed_core.name: taxable_status
typed_core.why: processor — taxable vs reimbursement affects gross-up
typed_core.prompt_hint: Foster-care income is generally non-taxable difficulty-of-care payments; the taxable_status and reimbursement/income distinction matters for whether it counts and can be grossed up

typed_core.name: termination_or_change_events
typed_core.why: processor — pending changes that break continuance

typed_core.name: expected_continuance_statement
typed_core.why: processor — the 3-year-continuance test hinges on this

typed_core.name: verifier_name_title
typed_core.why: processor — who signed the verification; independence

nested_lists.name: payment_history
nested_lists.shape_reason: a verification typically lists 6-24 monthly payments; flat rows (period, amount, date_paid) stay well under the ceiling and support a future income-averaging / stability check

fields.name: amount
fields.why: the payment amount for the period

fields.name: date_paid
fields.why: when the period's payment was made

fields.name: source
fields.why: provenance snippet for the payment row

rejected.name: issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: agency_contact_phone covers the one contact a processor needs

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block, verifier_signature
rejected.reason: execution not rule-checked; verifier_name_title carries attribution

rejected.name: placement_identifier_masked
rejected.reason: OPTIONAL; duplicates the case number; adds PII surface with no consumer

rejected.name: reimbursement_vs_income_components
rejected.reason: second nested list; over budget — leave to catch-all

encoding_variations: gross_payment_amount / payment_frequency — '$620 biweekly', '$1,240/mo', '$40/day per child'; the amount is meaningless without the frequency and the per-child basis — carry both
expected_continuance_statement — prose ('payments expected to continue'), a checkbox, or a fixed end date; capture verbatim, do not infer a yes/no
taxable_status — 'non-taxable reimbursement' vs 'reportable income'; drives whether income can be grossed up

open_questions.q: taxable_status vs reimbursement_vs_income_components — the taxable/reimbursement split can be a single enum-degraded string or a nested breakdown.
open_questions.recommendation: keep the flat taxable_status; only nest reimbursement_vs_income_components if a rule must read component amounts GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: Child data minimization — the catalog has no child-identifier field, which is correct. Confirm the prompt hard-blocks child PII from the catch-all, since the catch-all is stored unmasked.
options: confirm prompt hard-blocks child PII from the catch-all
open_questions.recommendation: confirm the prompt hard-blocks the foster child's name, DOB, and case-child identifiers from every field including the catch-all GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): dependent_count only — no child names, ages, or DOBs (the prompt hard-blocks child PII).

notes: No rules consume this type today, so there is no rule floor; every field earns its place on identity, PII, processor use, or disambiguation.
case_provider_or_account_number_masked is restricted and pre-masked -> needs _PII_FIELDS registration (pre_masked true).
A foster-care verification concerns a child; no child name/DOB is a typed field, and the model must be told not to file child identifiers into the catch-all (unmasked).
Prompt hint (doc-level): do NOT extract the foster child's name, DOB, or case-child identifiers into any field including the catch-all.
gross_payment_amount is tagged 'headline' in the markdown, which is not one of the five reason_class values; mapped to processor and flagged as an ambiguity.
